utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an excellent question, sir. I did not reference it in the report. I looked at some of the authoritarian personality literature that came out right after World War II at the University of California. I didn't incorporate it, but they were certainly looking for the kind of man who could -- the authoritarian man who would be hypercathetic to these organising ideas, Naziism or whatever have you, and follow that blindly, so to speak; but at this point the status of the authoritarian personality and the research that went with it I think is by and large fallen by the wayside, but it's a very useful concept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: You in answering Judge Robinson saying that there are a strong compulsive features, and it's also in your report. Could you elaborate more about the type of compulsion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't mean compulsion in the sense of the kind of behaviors you might see with obsessive hand-washing and so on nor strong internal ruminations as obsessive compulsive disorder. I'm really talking about obsessive compulsive personality features, and that would be manifested in a number of ways. One was in the interview itself, he would often dilate on a number of what seemed to me very irrelevant details, but lots of details. It was very important to him to make sure that I got all the little details, so there was a hyper focus on minutia at the expense of the bigger picture. That's part of an obsessional character style. Also his defensive organisation was very much consistent with the obsessional character. Rationalisation, for example, these are higher lever neurotic-level defences. I'm speaking to a fellow psychoanalyst, I think. Sublimation, the things that you would expect to find with the obsessive character and then also the testing itself demonstrated yet another way to look at this, another facet of this. So when I start putting all this together, I'm really looking at a man who's quite obsessionally organised but not pathologically so. He's not to the point where he's engaging in obsessive compulsive behaviors which can be quite destructive to a person. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. May I finish, Your Honour, real quick?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, okay, just conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The long and the short of the quest for the Nazi personality is that it really became quite fruitless. There needed to be a way to find an alternative explanation for how do we understand these men? People began to look at things like the environment or social situations or the role that people were put in maybe as an alternative explanation for this kind of phenomena. There are a number of studies, kind of classic lines of research that came out of this. One of the ones that I looked at quite a bit was the Milgram studies. Stanley Milgram at Yale University -- these are Yale undergraduates, these are the cream of the cream, no legal history whatsoever, who would be encouraged --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are you saying in relation to the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. What I'm saying to the accused by and large is this is a man who's quite obedient to authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Alarid, you've spent the entire day, three sittings. I do not consider it in the interest of judicial economy to allow you to continue the examination-in-chief. You have had enough time. I want to deal with the question raised by the Prosecutor, I think, but then I need Ms. Sartorio first to tell me, how long will you be in cross-examination? Not as long as the examination-in-chief, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: At least two hours, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At least two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. I would like two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And who is your next witness, Mr. Alarid, after this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Clifford Jenkins, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. How long will that be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was hoping two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Two hours. Yes. And after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: For this week, we're hoping Mr. Rasic will be here. I don't know if we've gotten confirmation from VWS yet, but we were trying to arrange that. If not, Mr. Jenkins would be our final witness of the week and that I would be calling. The issue of -- except for the subpoenas, which are still in play. Other than that, Your Honour, the only loose end would be Dr. Andersen, and who's -- like I said, his testimony was blocked by the Department of Defence upon some impetus, and so we would be making a motion simply for the report to come in as based on for what weight it serves the Court, and that would be our position with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you said you were going to submit a motion on the 92 quater.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. I just haven't had time. I was hoping to -- I find we're going to have a double session tomorrow and I was hopefully going to do it in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, there's no double session. We are sitting --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. It was on the calendar, so I was worried about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so there's no ambiguity, it seems that something Mr. Alarid said except for the subpoenas, am I to take it Milan Lukic will not be testifying; if it's still planned to call him, when would that be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It would be at the end, and we haven't proofed him. I haven't had time to spend much time in the gaol with him during this experts week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, did you have any other mater to raise with this witness? And if so, what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The only thing I was going to ask him to extrapolate on and I'm not sure what time it would take, would be why Milgram and its progeny are so important to the war crime scenarios that we might be experiencing relevant to this situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's Milgram?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Milgram was the report that he just referenced, Your Honour, and it's a set of studies and follow-up studies involving leadership and following orders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have asked him about leadership. That's the end of your examination-in-chief. Mr. Alarid, tomorrow Ms. Sartorio will begin her cross-examination. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It seems now that it will be impossible for the Prosecution to call any evidence on Friday. Am I correct? Can I tell Dr. Fagel that he should not try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was your estimate, Mr. Alarid? What advice would you give the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think just given Ms. Sartorio's opportunity and the next witness, I think that's a very reasonable assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just also state that I have no objection to taking it out of order, so if we're going to find ourselves with some free time on Friday, I'm happy enough to use it efficiently by calling Dr. Fagel. It's just it's hard for me to estimate whether we will have free time or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think realistically with us not having a double session, I think that's fair that the week is full.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe there is a double session on Friday, is there not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, there is a double session on Friday that he could use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's -- well, assuming Mr. Rasic is here, that would fill that time definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm reminded that the -- in the decision that we issued today, the calling of Dr. Fagel will be dependent on certain documents being produced by other witnesses, and those witnesses have not yet been called. Those are I think three witnesses who are to be called by you. Perhaps you haven't seen the decision in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, technically, that would be the proper order. It's also possible just to mark them for identification and then they never make their way into evidence until the foundation for them is established, but I'm happy to -- I'm just trying to offer suggestion for the Chamber to use the time efficiently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: One housekeeping, Your Honour. I sent a letter submission to the Chambers regarding Ms. Marie O'Leary having special permission to lead Clifford Jenkins. Marie O'Leary. She was my legal assistant and case manager. She sat to my left for the first part of the trial. I was going to give her the opportunity to examine our policeman, and if the Court would allow special dispensation for that fact, that's all we'd be asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why is there a special dispensation? Is she not an attorney?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: She is an attorney. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She is?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: She is. Of course. She's a licensed attorney since 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And she meets the standards of our Rule --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: She doesn't have her seven years of criminal law experience, but I think she's a competent attorney and can practice law before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you're always presenting these little problems. We'll have to deal with that. I can't give you an answer to that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I would say bring Dr. Fagel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
